reading.body:
DataBank Pittsburgh PIT2 publishes 5 MW of IT capacity, which could host between 125 and 500 racks depending on power density, but the operator has not disclosed which workload class this facility targets.

The gap between possible densities matters for AI. A facility designed for colocation at 10 kW per rack serves general enterprise customers and cannot run modern training clusters efficiently. The same power at 40 kW per rack signals AI-ready infrastructure, with redundancy and cooling sufficient for accelerator-heavy workloads. Without operator disclosure of power density, thermal design, or certifications, the facility's actual role in the compute supply chain is opaque.

Within Pennsylvania's published data, PIT2 ranks second at 5 MW of 11 MW total across two disclosed facilities. However, 12 of 14 mapped Pennsylvania facilities publish no capacity figures, so this ranking describes only a partial view. What appears locally significant is negligible by AI scaling standards, where individual hyperscale deployments routinely exceed this entire campus's capacity tenfold or more.
